findings: Multiple current public station observations identify DE*EDR EVSEs as E.ON Drive Germany GmbH.
Current station-level observations show 0.52 EUR/kWh on AC and 0.69 EUR/kWh on DC/HPC, with 0.10 EUR/min time fees after 240 minutes AC or 45 minutes DC at sampled sites.
The exact current direct/ad-hoc contract could not be established from an official E.ON public tariff page for every DEEDR EVSE; sampled third-party prices must not be promoted network-wide.
DEEDR.neededToComplete: Resolve E.ON's official public direct-payment/app station tariff payload or AFIR/Mobilithek exact tariff mapping for every DEEDR EVSE, including time/blocking rules and validity.

DEUFC.operator: shared/legacy prefix; E.ON Drive Infrastructure plus other physical operators
findings: DE*UFC is not safe as a single physical-CPO tariff key. A 2026 station in Heilbronn is identified as E.ON Drive Infrastructure, while DE*UFC*E01269*1/2 are identified as Stadtwerke Geldern GmbH.

Current station-level prices also differ by physical operator: sampled E.ON Drive HPC points are reported at 0.69 EUR/kWh, whereas the Stadtwerke Geldern DEUFC site is reported at 0.59 EUR/kWh plus 0.07 EUR/min blocking fee.
Therefore no DEUFC-wide tariff may be inferred; physical-operator and EVSE-level resolution is mandatory.
DEUFC.neededToComplete: Resolve every DEUFC EVSE to its physical CPO from BNetzA/AFIR/Mobilithek and attach only that operator's exact station tariff, including blocking fees.

findings: BNetzA/Mobilithek-derived station pages consistently identify DE*WAT EVSEs as Wattif Europe GmbH / Wattif Germany.
Wattif's official German site exposes a charger map and describes itself as operating and billing charging infrastructure rather than publishing one universal driver tariff.
Public station evidence shows at least one Wattif site with a 0.65 EUR/kWh ad-hoc price, but this is insufficient to extrapolate across the DEWAT catalog.
DEWAT.neededToComplete: Harvest the exact Wattif app/QR/direct-payment tariff for each DEWAT site/EVSE or obtain an official station-level feed; preserve any site-set energy, time, parking or blocking components.

DEGUC.operator: Grid & Co. GmbH / Gridware platform; multiple physical operators
findings: Grid & Co. officially describes Gridware as a multi-tenant software platform for CPOs and EMPs, so DE*GUC must not be assumed to represent one retail tariff authority.
DE*GUC EVSE identifiers embed multiple downstream operator codes, including RWG (REWAG/Stadtwerke Kelheim context), EAM and BEC, confirming shared-platform behavior.

REWAG officially publishes its own direct-payment tariffs (0.50 EUR/kWh below 50 kW and 0.55 EUR/kWh from 50 kW, with defined blocking fees), while other DEGUC sub-operators require their own exact pricing.
DEGUC.neededToComplete: Resolve each DEGUC EVSE to its physical CPO/sub-operator and apply only exact operator/site tariffs from official QR/app surfaces or AFIR/Mobilithek station-level data. Never use a DEGUC-wide fallback.

guardrails: No sampled aggregator tariff is promoted to a network-wide tariff.
Shared platform prefixes are resolved by physical operator and EVSE before pricing.
Unknown station-level direct prices remain fail-closed.
